Article Title: Michael Dell's son Zach co-founded Base Power in 2023; it is now valued at $13 billion and has installed more than 23,000 home batteries
Article Text:
Diverse business models

The three-year-old company just locked down a $1 billion funding round that brings its valuation to $13 billion

Battery storage boom

His father helped put a computer in millions of homes. Now, Zach Dell wants to put a battery in them. The son of Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell, has co-founded a startup hoped to become America's next big power company. Base Power is racing to build and install tens of thousands of batteries in residential backyards and become one of the country's largest developers of battery storage. The three-year-old company just locked down a $1 billion funding round that brings its valuation to $13 billion and has raised more than $2.5 billion in all.The funding round was led by Ribbit Capital, Addition, Valor Equity Partners and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group, which is part of the firm’s Security and Resiliency Initiative. Interestingly, Dell's own father is not a backer.Base has installed more than 23,000 batteries across Texas and the Chicago area, a market it entered earlier this year. “We have so much to do and so much room to grow, and we’re very early in the scope of the opportunity,” Dell said, adding that the company plans to enter more states and, eventually, international markets. It does roughly 100 installations a day and expects to double the count by the year-end.So far, it has about 550 megawatt-hours installed, equal to a large, utility-sized storage project.Base functions on two business models. In deregulated markets, the company owns and operates the batteries, acting as a retail power provider while offering lower-than-average electricity rates. When the grid operates normally, it aggregates the batteries to feed electricity back to the system during periods of peak demand. If an outage strikes, it provides backup power. Texas customers also can sign up for the retail electricity plan without a battery. It also partners with regulated or municipal utilities and electric cooperatives, which use the batteries to relieve the local grid bottlenecks, while customers get backup power.Customers receive either one or two battery packs. The original units provided about 25 kilowatt-hours of storage, while the new modules, being rolled out now, offer 39.2 kilowatt-hours. That translates to 36 hours of backup power for most homes. The systems sit near the electric meter and are about the size of an air-conditioning compressor unit.According to a WSJ report, the first installation conducted by the company about three years ago had the team scouring for an electrician on Craigslist, who ultimately charged a whopping $500 in cash. “It was a very ridiculous situation,” said Jared Greene, head of software and a founding engineer at the company, who is considered Base’s first employee. “I was there until midnight.” Now, the installation of its newest battery takes under an hour because it uses a pre-wired, modular design. Base has about 500 employees.It leases space in the former Austin American-Statesman building downtown but is building a factory where it plans to scale up production.The expansion is a part of the battery storage boom. In the first quarter, the U.S. installed 3.3 gigawatts of battery storage (the amount that could be delivered at once during peak demand), or 8.4 gigawatt-hours (the energy the battery can store and deliver over time), according to a report from the American Clean Power Association and Wood Mackenzie. Of that, the home battery segment installed 1.3 gigawatt-hours in the first quarter, an industry record.Batteries can soak up cheap power during times of low demand and discharge power when supplies are tight; they also help to keep the grid stable. While large projects dominate the industry, more companies are pursuing home batteries that can be added at a fast rate.In West Texas, El Paso Electric asked homeowners served by its most crowded feeders to volunteer to have Base batteries installed. It is testing about 9 megawatts of batteries to see how they can help with peak demand, system reliability and affordability. El Paso Electric owns the battery, which is installed on the utility side of the meter, but homeowners get the backup power and are paid a $250 incentive per battery.Chief Executive Kelly Tomblin said El Paso Electric thinks the batteries could help offset some more costly investments that would otherwise be needed to replace power lines or infrastructure at substations to handle the spikes in power demand on the hottest 10 to 15 summer days. The utility’s demand leaps from 1,000 megawatts in winter to more than 2,500 megawatts during heat waves. While the company has modelled the economics, this summer's tests will reveal if it expands the program to other crowded feeder lines.Antonio Gracias, the founder of Valor Equity Partners, said he likes the technology and team Dell is assembling. Base co-founder Justin Lopas is the former head of manufacturing at Anduril Industries, another Valor investment.“I think the problem they’re solving is really important and they have an interesting solution,” said Gracias, who was an early backer of Tesla and SpaceX. He added the U.S. needs more power if it is going to come back as a manufacturing powerhouse. “The limit of GDP growth ultimately will be the amount of energy available to produce things in America,” Gracias said.
Article Summary: Base Power is racing to build and install tens of thousands of batteries in residential backyards. The three-year-old company just locked down a $1 billion funding round that brings its valuation to $13 billion and has raised more than $2.5 billion in all.

Article Title: In Washington, Pumas are protecting human lives by preventing vehicle collisions accounting for a 76% reduction in accidents
Article Text:
They were 15% less likely to be near roads, choosing to spend time in remote habitat areas instead.

Whoever thought animals would be able to prevent accidents? According to a recent study published in 'Current Biology' the presence of pumas in Washington has decreased the risk of road collisions immensely. Researchers found that the presence of pumas in the Olympic Peninsula area of Washington has changed the behaviour of the local deer population, thus decreasing the animal-vehicle collisions and improving overall safety.In areas where pumas are present, there is a 76% reduction in the number of deer-vehicle collisions because deer shift activity toward daylight hours. “We found that large carnivores can make roadways safer through their effects on prey behaviour and space use,” Justin Suraci of Conservation Science Partners in Truckee, Calif., the study’s lead author, said in a press release.“Deer alter their use of both space and time where pumas are present, overlapping less with roads and reducing activity at night, when some of the most dangerous collisions occur,” Suraci added. “Increased road safety thus represents an ecosystem service that large predators like pumas can provide to human communities.”Since pumas serve as predators to deer, they steer clear of the roadways, in turn decreasing accidents.The study sought to find the benefits of living in close proximity to larger predatory animals like pumas in developed areas. Deer were more active during the day in areas where pumas are present, the researchers found.They were 15% less likely to be near roads, choosing to spend time in remote habitat areas instead. The change in deer behaviour led to a 67% reduction “in the likelihood of a deer-vehicle collision,” researchers found, according to the press release.Pumas, also known as cougars or mountain lions are the largest wild cats in Washington. They are known for their strength, agility and ability to jump, as per the Washington Department of Fish & Wildlife. The large cats typically use “steep canyons, rock outcroppings and boulders, or vegetation, such as dense brush and forests, to remain hidden while hunting,” per the agency’s official website.According to a 2025 study published in Global Ecology and Conservation , every year in the USA, approximately 1.5 to 2.1 million deer-vehicle collisions occur, leading to 200-400 human fatalities, 26,000–59,000 human injuries, and greater than $10 billion in property damage.Thus, researchers hope that the study will help people see the benefits of living among large carnivores, according to the press release. “When we talk about pumas, we often focus on the risks they pose. But we rarely stop to consider the many ways they benefit us as well,” Mark Elbroch of Panthera said in the press release. “Living alongside large carnivores isn’t simply about protecting wildlife; it’s about protecting the many ways they quietly benefit us every day. ”
Article Summary: Researchers found that the presence of pumas in the Olympic Peninsula area of Washington has changed the behaviour of the local deer population. They were 15% less likely to be near roads, choosing to spend time in remote habitat areas instead. The change in deer behaviour led to a 67% reduction “in the likelihood of a deer-vehicle collision,” researchers found.

Article Title: Pentagon strips ex-Air Force secretary Kendall of security clearance over Air Force One claim
Article Text: Former Air Force secretary Frank Kendall has been stripped of his security clearance and barred from from holding “any sensitive position," after the Pentagon accused him of sharing classified details about Air Force One's capabilities with the media.Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell announced the action on Friday, saying it was effective immediately. “Effective immediately, the Department of War has REVOKED former Secretary of the Air Force Frank Kendall’s eligibility for access to classified information and his ability to hold any sensitive position,” Parnell wrote on X.Parnell did not identify the outlet Kendall allegedly shared the information with. Kendall told news agency AP late Friday that he was “completely mystified” by the revocation.The move follows reporting last month, including by The New York Times, about security concerns surrounding the new Air Force One aircraft gifted by Qatar. The aircraft underwent a $400 million retrofit and has been used domestically, while US president Donald Trump also flew on it to Turkey last month.“I’ve always been extremely careful to not say anything classified, and as far as I know I have not,” Kendall told AP, adding, “No one has said anything to me about what I’m asserted to have revealed and I can’t imagine what it could be.”The Times reported last month that the new aircraft lacked some of the advanced security features of the older Air Force One jets. Two former Air Force officials told the newspaper they were surprised Trump had used the new aircraft overseas, where security risks were greater.Kendall, who served under former president Joe Biden, was quoted by The New York Times as saying, “Time didn’t permit all the normal Air Force One modifications, so some mix of security, communications and support is missing.”“With the Iran situation, this could be of concern,” Kendall said. “Frankly, I’m surprised to see this plane used outside the U.S.”Kendall had been in charge of the Air Force when the department was pressing Boeing to accelerate its delayed contract for two new Air Force One aircraft. He later told US media organisations that the Qatari aircraft would have required three to four years of modifications to meet the standards of the older Boeing 747s.Trump flew the Qatari aircraft to Turkey for a Nato summit but later switched to an older Air Force One aircraft to leave the summit as the US launched airstrikes on Iran and Tehran attacked three Gulf Arab states.Trump reportedly made the switch at the urging of the Secret Service. He later denied that the change was prompted by security concerns, while saying he was under threat “all the time” and was Iran’s “No. 1” target.The Air Force has defended the rapid conversion of the aircraft, saying it was carried out “without accepting any risk regarding security, safety, or secure communications”. It has, however, acknowledged differences in the aircraft’s capabilities.The Air Force said “several highly complex engineering modifications” required for the new US-made Air Force One aircraft were deliberately excluded from the Qatari jet’s conversion. It also acknowledged that the aircraft did not receive wider exit doors or multiple stairs built into its hull.The dispute has also drawn attention to the government’s handling of media reporting on the aircraft. The Justice Department subpoenaed New York Times reporters seeking to compel them to identify sources behind the reporting. The subpoenas were withdrawn last month after criticism from a judge over the department’s legal work.Parnell said the Pentagon considered protection of classified information a fundamental obligation. “Safeguarding classified information is a non-negotiable duty,” he wrote. “Those who violate that trust forfeit the privilege of access and any role requiring it.”However, this is not an isolated incident, the Trump administration has previously revoked security clearances from current and former national security officials. Parnell did not say whether Kendall’s case would be referred for prosecution, and the Pentagon did not immediately respond to questions on the matter.Such allegations can lead to criminal referrals over suspected violations of the Espionage Act.The Obama administration had charged former intelligence contractor Edward Snowden after he leaked US surveillance secrets and fled to Russia. More recently, a Massachusetts Air National Guard member received 15 years in prison in 2024 for leaking classified Ukraine war documents, described as a major national security breach.
Article Summary: Former Air Force secretary Frank Kendall has been stripped of his security clearance and barred from from holding “any sensitive position” The Pentagon accused him of sharing classified details about Air Force One's capabilities with the media. Kendall said he was “completely mystified” by the revocation.

Article Title: Sanchez vs Meloni: Spain imposes Italy border checks as Ceuta migrant row escalates
Article Text:
Sanchez, Meloni clash over Ceuta migrant influx as Schengen dispute escalates

Spain has imposed temporary border checks on air and sea travel from Italy as tensions between the two EU countries escalate over migration. Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez and his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni appeared at odds over the EU’s migration policy.According to the BBC, Spain’s checks began at midnight and will remain in place until September 7, unless the situation changes. The move came a week after Italy introduced similar restrictions following the arrival of around 78,000 migrants from Morocco into Spain’s North African exclave of Ceuta.Spain had asked Italy to withdraw its checks by Sunday, but Rome said the measures would remain until at least August 15. Italy said it expected another possible wave of migration towards Ceuta around that time.The dispute has brought Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni into a fresh clash over migration policy. Meloni has long pushed for tighter EU migration controls.Italy does not share a land border with Spain. Rome said it temporarily suspended parts of the Schengen rules for non-EU nationals arriving from Spain to prevent migrants who entered Ceuta from travelling onwards to Italy.Madrid rejected the reasoning, calling it based on “spurious arguments” and saying migrants who entered Ceuta had no route into the Schengen area.Italy also said it would not accept what it described as “ultimatums”. Rome said the checks would remain until security and terrorism risks had been fully addressed. Spanish citizens are exempt from the additional checks, which mainly apply to non-EU nationals.However, the BBC reported that some Italian airports have seen long queues, with passengers arriving from Spain being directed to separate lines for checks.Spain’s new measures include passport, nationality and visa checks for passengers arriving from Italy. Madrid said the controls were necessary because of continued “irregular migratory pressure”.Most of the migrants who entered Ceuta last week were sent back within days, but nearly 1,400 minors remain there. Spain has not confirmed that another large-scale crossing is expected, although social media posts in Morocco have fuelled concerns about a possible second attempt.Spanish authorities said they were monitoring the situation but did not expect a repeat of last week’s events.The reason behind the sudden arrival of tens of thousands of migrants remains unclear. EU Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner has blamed criminal networks for spreading disinformation, a view also supported by Spain.The crossings followed a Spanish Supreme Court ruling that migrants intercepted at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be immediately returned to Morocco.Morocco has criticised the ruling, saying it weakened the system meant to deter migrants from attempting the crossing.Ceuta and Melilla, two Spanish enclaves in North Africa, have long been a source of tension between Spain and Morocco, which does not recognise Spanish sovereignty over them.
Article Summary: Spain has imposed temporary border checks on air and sea travel from Italy. Move came a week after Italy introduced similar restrictions following the arrival of around 78,000 migrants from Morocco into Spain’s North African exclave of Ceuta. Spain had asked Italy to withdraw its checks by Sunday, but Rome said the measures would remain until at least August 15.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Thomas Aquinas: 'Better to illuminate than merely to shine, to deliver to others...' and the case for sharing what you know before it dies with you
Article Text:
Thomas Aquinas was a 13th-century theologian and philosopher whose work combined Christian theology with Aristotelian philosophy

"Better to illuminate than merely to shine, to deliver to others contemplated truths than merely to contemplate."

A medieval friar rethinking the monastic life

The philosophy of overflowing wisdom

Translating deep work into public value

An intellectual sitting alone in a room may reach brilliant conclusions, but if those ideas never leave the desk, they remain unused. A candle burning inside a locked box lights only the box while leaving the hallway outside in darkness.This contrast between keeping wisdom to yourself and sharing it with others is at the heart of a famous idea from the thirteenth century:The quote describes two different ways of living. Simply shining represents personal brilliance, an impressive display that asks nothing from others except admiration. Illuminating, however, helps other people see the world more clearly. It treats knowledge not as something to keep for yourself, but as a light meant to help everyone better understand reality.The idea remains powerful because it speaks to a basic human struggle between personal growth and public responsibility. Intelligence, expertise, and deep study can easily become self-focused pursuits. The quote reminds us that the real purpose of gaining knowledge is not personal success, but helping others understand a complicated world.Italian philosopher, theologian, and Dominican friar Thomas Aquinas wrote these words in his great work, Summa Theologiae. Written between 1265 and 1274, the Summa was intended as a complete guide to Christian theology and Aristotelian philosophy for students and Dominican friars.To understand why Aquinas wrote this line, it helps to understand the debate that divided medieval religious orders. For centuries, the highest spiritual ideal in Western Europe was the contemplative life followed by monastic orders such as the Benedictines. Monks withdrew from society into isolated monasteries, spending their lives in prayer, meditation, and study, away from the distractions of the outside world.In the early thirteenth century, a different type of religious order appeared. The mendicants, including the Dominicans and Franciscans, lived among ordinary people instead of behind monastery walls. Founded by Saint Dominic in 1216, the Dominican Order focused on preaching and teaching in towns and universities.Critics argued that public preaching weakened the spiritual purity that came from silent contemplation. In Summa Theologiae (Secunda Secundae, Question 188, Article 6), Aquinas defended the Dominican mission. He compared the active life with the contemplative life and concluded that combining the two was better than choosing either one alone.The original Latin phrase, Sicut enim maius est illuminare quam lucere solum, ita maius est contemplata aliis tradere quam solum contemplari, became the defining statement of the Dominican mission. The shorter phrase Contemplata aliis tradere ("to hand down to others the fruits of contemplation") remains one of the order's main mottos today.At the heart of Aquinas's argument is the difference between quietly gaining knowledge and generously sharing it. Contemplation requires patience, discipline, and deep thought to understand difficult truths. Aquinas never questioned its importance. In fact, he argued that teaching without first thinking deeply becomes empty words.However, Aquinas believed that stopping with personal enlightenment leaves the journey unfinished. Wisdom is not meant to be stored away like wealth. When someone truly understands an important truth, that knowledge should naturally lead to action.This idea builds on Aristotle's concept of eudaimonia (human flourishing), which argues that people reach their full potential by acting within a community rather than living in isolation. It also reflects Plato's allegory of the cave. The philosopher who leaves the cave and sees the sunlight cannot simply enjoy the view alone. He has a moral duty to return and help others find their way out of the darkness.Aquinas presented teaching, mentoring, and public discussion not as distractions from intellectual life, but as its highest purpose. Sharing knowledge means turning difficult ideas into clear language, testing them through public discussion, and using them to solve real human problems.The difference between shining and illuminating still offers an important lesson for modern work, leadership, and media.In business, leaders often focus on shining by building personal brands, collecting achievements, and making public statements that highlight their own abilities. Good leadership, however, is about illumination. When Satya Nadella became CEO of Microsoft in 2014, he changed the company's culture from one of "know-it-alls" to one of "learn-it-alls." The focus shifted away from individual brilliance toward creating systems that helped every employee improve.The academic and scientific world faces a similar challenge. Thousands of research papers are published every year behind expensive paywalls and written in technical language that most people cannot understand. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many immunologists stepped away from their laboratories to write clear public health guides. By doing so, they moved beyond contemplation and helped fight misinformation with useful facts.In education, the quote shows the difference between an expert who uses complicated language to impress students and a teacher who explains difficult ideas simply enough for students to understand on their own. The late physicist Richard Feynman strongly supported this principle, arguing that if you cannot explain an idea in simple terms to a freshman, then you do not fully understand it yourself.Aquinas's standard suggests that the real measure of expertise is not how impressive it appears, but how clearly it helps others understand the path ahead.
Article Summary: Thomas Aquinas was a 13th-century theologian and philosopher. His work combined Christian theology with Aristotelian philosophy. He argued that the real purpose of gaining knowledge is not personal success, but helping others understand a complicated world.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Ernest Hemingway: 'Always do sober what you said you'd do drunk. That will teach you to keep your mouth shut' and a funny lesson on self-discipline
Article Text:
Quote of the Day ​by Ernest Hemingway

Funny take on drunken boasting

Man of his word

American writer Ernest Hemingway was a man famous for living a life of intense action, bold words, and heavy drinking. He spent his years fighting in wars, hunting big game, fishing in open seas, and writing classic novels. Along the way, he developed a reputation for being a tough guy who held himself and others to a strict personal code. One of his most famous quotes captures his attitude toward honesty, personal accountability, and alcohol: "Always do sober what you said you'd do drunk. That will teach you to keep your mouth shut."When Charles Scribner (IV) succeeded his late father as head of the country’s most venerable publishing firm in 1952, Ernest Hemingway wrote him a long personal letter, which concluded with a list of his “rules for life.” This quote was one of them.This quote sounds like a funny piece of practical advice for anyone who has ever consumed one too many drinks at a party. Drinking alcohol lowers a person's inhibitions. It melts away fear, self-doubt, and caution. Under the influence, people often feel bolder, richer, smarter, and stronger than they actually are. In that relaxed state, it is easy to make wild promises, pick fights, volunteer for hard tasks, or boast about things you intend to do.A person might promise to help a friend move across the country, pledge a huge sum of money, or agree to run a marathon, all while sipping a glass of whiskey in a room full of cheering friends.The problem comes the next morning. When the alcohol wears off, reality sets in. The false confidence disappears, leaving behind a headache and a sense of dread. The standard human response in that situation is to make excuses. Most people will call their friend, laugh off the promise as a silly joke, and apologize for having too much to drink. They try to escape the commitment by using alcohol as an excuse for their foolishness.Hemingway utterly rejected that easy exit. His advice demands that you force yourself to fulfill every single promise you made, no matter how uncomfortable, expensive, or painful it might be. If you promised while drunk that you would climb a mountain, you must wake up, put on your boots, and go climb that mountain. If you promised to give someone money, you hand over the cash. If you promised to take on a difficult task, you show up and do the work.The second part of the quote explains why this harsh rule is necessary: "That will teach you to keep your mouth shut." Forcing yourself to suffer through the consequences of your own loose talk is a form of painful discipline. Once you have to spend a miserable weekend following through on a foolish commitment you made during a late night at the bar, you learn a hard lesson. The sheer misery of paying for your big mouth cures you of the habit of making empty promises. Next time you hold a glass in your hand and feel the urge to brag or make a grand pledge, the memory of that pain will stop you in your tracks. You will choose to stay quiet instead.This philosophy fits perfectly with Hemingway's life and his personal view of manhood and honor. Hemingway lived through severe injuries in World War I, survived plane crashes, and dealt with constant physical pain. He believed deeply that a person's character is defined by how they act when things get hard. He had zero respect for people who talked big but shrank away when it came time to act. To Hemingway, a man’s word had to mean something. If your word only counts when it is convenient for you, then your word is completely worthless. Using alcohol as an excuse to break a promise was, in his eyes, a form of cowardice.Hemingway's rule is not just about drinking alcohol. It is really a universal lesson about self-control and personal accountability. Alcohol simply acts as a magnifying glass for a common human weakness, which is speaking before thinking. People make silly commitments sober all the time out of a desire to impress others, to avoid saying no, or to feel important in the moment. They promise favours they do not have time to deliver, or they take on extra work just to look good in front of a boss.When you hold yourself to a strict standard of carrying out every single commitment you speak aloud, you quickly realize how dangerous loose words can be. You learn that words carry real weight and real consequences. The ultimate goal of Hemingway's rule is to teach us self-restraint. It forces us to slow down, control our impulses, and protect our personal integrity. Silence is usually better than a foolish promise. By learning to keep your mouth shut until you actually mean what you say, you save yourself from useless regret and build a reputation as someone whose word can truly be trusted.
Article Summary: Ernest Hemingway was famous for living a life of intense action, bold words, and heavy drinking. One of his most famous quotes captures his attitude toward honesty, personal accountability, and alcohol. "Always do sober what you said you'd do drunk. That will teach you to keep your mouth shut"

Article Title: Quote of the day by Warren Buffett: 'The most important thing to do if you find yourself in a hole is to stop digging' and a useful business lesson
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Warren Buffett.

The trap of digging a hole

Why do we keep on digging the hole? We hate wasting

What is the life lesson?

Among the vast collection of aphorisms attributed to Warren Buffett , few are as blunt or practical as his famous rule of self-correction: "The most important thing to do if you find yourself in a hole is to stop digging." While the statement sounds like simple common sense, it addresses one of the most destructive tendencies in human psychology and business management: the refusal to admit a mistake and cut losses before a bad situation turns into a catastrophic failure.Buffett explained this idea in a 1990 letter to the shareholders of his company, Berkshire Hathaway. He was talking about insurance executives who kept lowering their prices and taking huge financial risks, even though they were losing money. Instead of stepping back, they kept pushing forward and making their problems worse.Buffett understood this trap because he had fallen into it himself earlier in his life. Early in his career, he liked to buy struggling, beaten-down companies for a very low price, hoping to squeeze out one last bit of profit. In 1962, he bought a failing textile company named Berkshire Hathaway.He thought he could turn the company around or make a quick profit.But the American textile industry was dying, and the business kept losing money. Instead of walking away, Buffett spent years putting more and more money into the factory, buying new equipment and trying to keep it alive.Eventually, he realized he was just pouring good money after bad. He was digging his own hole deeper. Buffett finally decided to stop. He stopped putting money into the failing textile mills and used that cash to buy great, healthy businesses instead—like insurance companies, newspaper publishers, and Coca-Cola. That single decision turned a failing factory into one of the most successful companies in history.The reason people keep "digging" comes down to a simple mind trap: we hate wasting what we've already spent. Once you put a lot of money, time, or pride into something, it is hard to give up. You feel like quitting means all your past effort was wasted. So, a person might stay with a bad stock, a company might keep funding a failed product, or someone might stay in the wrong career just because they already put so many years into it.Stopping the digging takes courage and honesty. It means swallowing your pride and admitting that a plan did not work out.Buffett may have unknowingly given us the best life lesson in the simplest words. Meant to be business advice, this quote teaches us how to navigate difficult life situations as well. Instead of pondering over it and getting dragged into the whirlwind of negativity, the first step is to get out of it. The advice does not mention how to get out of it but leaves hint. If you find yourself in a hole and there is no way out, then at least don't go down further. Stop whatever you are doing as that's the action responsible for putting you in the hole.Buffett's advice reminds us that everyone makes mistakes. The smartest people aren't the ones who never mess up; they are the ones who recognize a bad situation, put down the shovel, cut their losses, and move on.
Article Summary: Warren Buffett: "The most important thing to do if you find yourself in a hole is to stop digging" Buffett understood this trap because he had fallen into it himself earlier in his life. He stopped putting money into the failing textile mills and used that cash to buy great, healthy businesses.

Article Title: Video: 2 injured after gunman opens fire near New York subway station
Article Text:
NYPD said a 20-year-old and a 31-year-old man were injured in the Bronx shooting.

Two men were injured after a gunman opened fire near a busy subway station in New York City's Bronx on Thursday evening, NY police said.The shooting happened at around 6 p.m. outside the West Farms Square-E Tremont Avenue subway station. Surveillance footage from the area showed a man wearing a white hoodie walking towards a plaza before firing several shots in the direction of a group gathered near a shop.Video from the scene also captured people fleeing as the gunman escaped. One man was seen tumbling over a bench and rolling onto the pavement, although it was not immediately clear whether he had been hit by gunfire.According to the New York Police Department (NYPD), a 20-year-old man was shot in the leg, while a 31-year-old man suffered a gunshot wound to the buttocks.Both victims were taken to St. Barnabas Hospital, where they were reported to be in stable condition.Police have not confirmed whether the two injured men were the intended targets or were caught in the gunfire by chance.The suspect fled the scene after the shooting. No arrests had been announced as of Thursday night, and the investigation remains ongoing.
Article Summary: The shooting happened at around 6 p.m. outside the West Farms Square-E Tremont Avenue subway station in New York City's Bronx. A 20-year-old man was shot in the leg, while a 31-year old man suffered a gunshot wound to the buttocks. Both victims were taken to St Barnabas Hospital, where they were reported to be in stable condition.

Article Title: PhD student Vikram Mubayi found dead in lake after going missing on solo hiking trip in US
Article Text:
UC Santa Barbara PhD student Vikram Mubayi was found dead after going missing during a solo hike in California's Inyo National Forest.

Vikram Mubayi, a chemical engineering PhD student at the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB), was found dead on August 3 in California's Inyo National Forest, two days after he went missing during a solo hiking trip in the Big Pine Lakes area.According to local reports, Mubayi last contacted his family on the evening of August 1 before a search operation was launched by Inyo County Search & Rescue.Authorities later recovered Mubayi's body from Big Pine Lakes, and officials said the circumstances surrounding his death remain under investigation, with no indication of foul play.Born and raised in Hong Kong, Mubayi was described by his family as an experienced hiker.In a post on Reddit, his sibiling urged people to inform if someone had seen Vikram. "My brother Vikram is 6’3, 170lbs, dark hair, and has been out of contact since 8.30pm yesterday in the big pine lakes area in the eastern sierra, specifically around agassiz col. Have attached a link to his route here strava.com/routes/3516945857263630584. Did anyone happen to see him along the way? he last sent an update 8.37PM PST from the following coordinates: 37.10942° N, 118.52428° W" the post said."He’s a fairly experienced hiker and we think that he reached a reasonably easy part of the route, so would have expected him back by now. his car is still at the trailhead. So sorry if this is not the right place to post. can post somewhere else if there’s a better place," it added.The official confirmation is yet to come from the authorities.
Article Summary: Vikram Mubayi, a chemical engineering PhD student at the University of California, Santa Barbara, was found dead on August 3 in California's Inyo National Forest. The circumstances surrounding his death remain under investigation, with no indication of foul play.

Iran president says he heard a voice, not saw a face in secret Khamenei meeting

Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian was reportedly taken to a secret location in Tehran and granted only a brief meeting with a man introduced as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, according to Iran International.The reported encounter, conducted inside a dark, tinted-window vehicle, has fuelled fresh questions over the secrecy surrounding Iran's leadership.According to the report, Pezeshkian was unable to see the man seated beside him and later questioned whether the voice he heard had indeed belonged to the country's new supreme leader.Their account of what they described as the only known meeting between the president and Iran's third supreme leader differs markedly from Pezeshkian's public version of events.Speaking at a gathering of trade association representatives in mid-May, Pezeshkian said he had spent two and a half hours with the new leader in what he described as a "cordial atmosphere."However, the report said that the meeting lasted only a few minutes, after which the president was asked to leave.According to the report, the meeting took place only after Pezeshkian repeatedly sought an audience with the supreme leader and threatened to resign.They said the leader's office agreed to the meeting under pressure but informed the president that, unlike previous practice, he would not be received at the supreme leader's official residence.Instead, Pezeshkian's security team reportedly took him to an undisclosed location in Tehran, where he was escorted from his vehicle into the back seat of a dark, tinted-window commercial car. The report claimed the supreme leader was already inside, but the vehicle was kept dark enough that the two men could not see each other. They also alleged that Khamenei's security personnel did not allow a handshake, and the conversation took place entirely by voice.The reported arrangement left Pezeshkian feeling humiliated, as per the report.Officials in the president's office told Iran International that he later questioned whether the person beside him had actually been the supreme leader, as he had only heard a voice during the brief meeting.Pezeshkian had earlier acknowledged that communicating with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is "very difficult.""It is very difficult to communicate with him at the moment, but in any case, his presence is a very great source of strength for us so that we can continue," Pezeshkian said.Mojtaba Khamenei has continued to issue written statements, but his absence from public view since assuming Iran's top leadership has fuelled speculation about his relationship with senior officials and his whereabouts. Nearly five months after the Assembly of Experts selected him to succeed his father as supreme leader, no audio recording or video of him has been released.The prolonged silence has also drawn attention in Iran's state-aligned media. On Sunday, the Hamshahri newspaper's website published a video claiming that foreign intelligence agencies could use advanced acoustic analysis of audio recordings, including background noise, electrical grid frequency signatures and vocal characteristics, to identify the leader's location or assess his physical condition.The claims appeared to deepen, rather than dispel, speculation surrounding Khamenei's status.Conflicting assessments have also emerged internationally. Three weeks ago, US President Donald Trump said there was a "90 percent" chance that Mojtaba Khamenei had been killed, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has more recently said the Iranian leader is alive.
Article Summary: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian was reportedly taken to a secret location in Tehran and granted only a brief meeting with a man introduced as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. The reported encounter, conducted inside a dark, tinted-window vehicle, has fuelled fresh questions over the secrecy surrounding Iran's leadership.

Article Title: Watch: Scared Thailand school students duck under desks as gunshots ring out; 8 dead
Article Text:
Video shows Thailand students hiding under desks during school shooting (Image: X@/CatchUpFeed)

At least eight people were killed on Friday after a student opened fire at a school in Thailand before turning the gun on himself, a national police official said.The gunman first shot and killed his grandparents at their home before opening fire at the school.The student fired 26 rounds, while another 34 rounds of ammunition were recovered from the scene, according to a police statement.Videos from the scene showed students ducking under their desks as gunshots could be heard in the background.The shooting took place at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi province, northwest of Bangkok. Police identified the shooter as a student.Lt Col Dechrapee Kongdee, commander of the Nonthaburi Provincial Police, confirmed the casualties to Reuters and said the suspected gunman had died by suicide.He said those injured included one teacher and three students.An 18-year-old student said he initially mistook the sound of gunfire for firecrackers going off or someone banging an object."I didn't think ⁠it was a gun at first," he was quoted as saying by Reuters. "There were many shots: bang bang bang. Then it went quiet. Then it started again."According to district authorities, the school had around 3,100 students and 147 teachers enrolled during the 2025 academic year.The latest incident comes months after a teacher was killed and a student injured in a separate shooting at a school in Hat Yai district in southern Thailand in February.
Article Summary: Shooting took place at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Bang Kruai district, northwest of Bangkok. Gunman first shot and killed his grandparents at their home before opening fire at the school. Video shows students ducking under their desks as gunshots can be heard in background.

Article Title: Exiled Bangladeshi cricket star Shakib Al Hasan willing to return, face murder trial if safety assured
Article Text:
Bangladesh cricket star Shakib Al Hasan, an exiled ally of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina, says he is ready to return home and face trial on murder charges if the government guarantees his security.

Bangladesh cricket Shakib Al Hasan has said he is willing to return home and face criminal proceedings against him if the government guarantees his safety, according to an exclusive interview with Reuters.Shakib has been living in exile in the United States since former prime minister Sheikh Hasina was ousted in a student-led uprising in August 2024. The former Bangladesh captain, who was also an Awami League lawmaker under Hasina, has not returned home since.“If I get the clearance from the government that my security will be ensured, I am happy to go back, face the court trial and everything that's needed to be done,” Shakib told Reuters by phone from Sri Lanka.He said he believed the allegations against him were baseless and wanted the opportunity to return and defend himself in court. Shakib said he was also keen to speak with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman about his return.Shakib is facing two active cases in Bangladesh. One concerns the alleged killing of a protester during the 2024 uprising, while another was filed by anti-corruption authorities. He said the murder case was filed on a day when he was playing a match in Toronto.Shakib also said his bank accounts had been frozen for around 18 months while investigations continued. He has not appointed a defence lawyer in the murder case, according to Reuters.His political links remain a major obstacle to his return. Shakib defended his decision to appear virtually at a press conference with Hasina in Delhi this week, saying he had only called for peace and progress in Bangladesh. He said he had no intention of distancing himself from Hasina or the Awami League to facilitate his return.The Rahman government, however, has rejected any suggestion of special treatment. His press secretary A.A.M. Saleh told Reuters that Shakib was facing the consequences of his association with the former government and that Bangladeshi law applied equally to everyone.“Shakib Al Hasan is an accused person, and he must surrender before the courts of Bangladesh to face the judicial process,” Saleh said.Shakib said he had previously tried to return. In late 2024, he boarded a flight home after receiving assurances that he would be protected, but was reportedly instructed to turn around while the plane was in transit. He returned to New York after landing in Dubai.A subsequent attempt also failed after he posted a birthday message for Hasina, which authorities cited as a reason for preventing his entry, he said.Despite the political and legal uncertainty, Shakib has not retired from international cricket. He said he wants to play a farewell series at home and hopes to represent Bangladesh at the 2027 ODI World Cup, although he acknowledged that he cannot continue indefinitely.“I am feeling good, still enjoying the game, playing well also,” Shakib told Reuters. “But ... age is not on my side at this moment, so I cannot wait for too long.”The cricketer also said he has not seen his parents in Bangladesh for two years and that the prolonged separation had been difficult for his family.
Article Summary: Bangladesh cricket star Shakib Al Hasan says he is willing to return home and face criminal proceedings against him if the government guarantees his safety. Shakib has been living in exile in the United States since former prime minister Sheikh Hasina was ousted in a student-led uprising in August 2024. The former Bangladesh captain, who was also an Awami League lawmaker under Hasina, has not returned home since.

Article Title: US sanctions Dubai-based crypto exchange over alleged Iran sanctions evasion and IRGC funding
Article Text:
An investigation found that the exchange had moved cryptocurrency on behalf of Iran's central bank, one of the world's largest illegal online gambling networks

The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on Dubai-based cryptocurrency exchange Shelbit, its founder Siavash Kayvanpour and a network of associated companies. It alleged that the company processed millions of dollars in digital assets for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Iran's central bank and other entities linked to the Iranian state.The US treasury department announced the action as part of a wider crackdown on sanctions evasion through cryptocurrency networks. It also sanctioned Aban Tether, an Iran-based crypto exchange, accusing it of processing millions of dollars in transactions for sanctioned Iranian entities, including Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange.Announcing the measures, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said, "Treasury will hunt down and dismantle the illicit financial networks that keep the regime afloat."A Reuters investigation published on July 31 identified Shelbit as the hub of a $4 billion Iranian sanctions evasion network. The report also said that the exchange had moved cryptocurrency on behalf of Iran's central bank, one of the world's largest illegal online gambling networks and wallet addresses linked by the Israeli government to the IRGC.The US treasury accused Kayvanpour of providing material support to both the IRGC and Nobitex.The United States had already sanctioned Nobitex on June 2 for allegedly enabling the Iranian government to circumvent Western sanctions.According to Reuters, tens of millions of dollars that passed through Shelbit came from a suspected Iranian bitcoin mining operation, while millions more were linked to an illegal gambling network run by two prominent Iranian social media influencers. Referring to the gambling operation, the Treasury said, "The Iranian regime's willingness to allow this gambling network to operate highlights its hypocrisy and corruption. "Although Shelbit's website had been inaccessible for months, preventing customers from carrying out transactions, Reuters reported that the exchange continued processing funds even during the recent US and Israeli military campaign against Iran. The website reappeared the day after the Reuters investigation was published.In a statement posted on its reactivated website on August 1, Shelbit denied the allegations. "Shelbit LLC categorically rejects any suggestion that the company knowingly participated in money laundering, terrorist financing, illegal gambling activity, sanctions evasion, or activity on behalf of any sanctioned, military, or governmental organisation," it said. The company added that it had ceased operations in January 2026.The US action comes shortly after Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority issued a notice stating that Shelbit violated anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing regulations.In a notice published on July 24, VARA said, "The exposure identified by VARA extends beyond consumer protection to more egregious cross-border transactions with the propensity to impact the integrity of the UAE financial system."
Article Summary: The United States imposed sanctions on Dubai-based cryptocurrency exchange Shelbit, its founder Siavash Kayvanpour and a network of associated companies. It alleged that the company processed millions of dollars in digital assets for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Iran's central bank and other entities linked to the Iranian state. A Reuters investigation identified Shelbit as the hub of a $4 billion Iranian sanctions evasion network.

Article Title: 'Don't be like Yasmin': US makes an example out of Venezuelan woman arrested by ICE, says you are illegal if...
Article Text:
75-year-old Texas businessman said Trump is breaking families after his 45-year-old fiancee was arrested by the ICE for visa overstay.

What is the case of Yasmin Suarez Reyes?

45-year-old Yasmin Suarez Reyes, a Venezuelan woman and a citizen of Spain, was arrested in July for overstaying her visa. Texas businessman John Gannon, 75, said he had been a lifelong Republican but now regreted voting for President Donald Trump as his fiancée is in ICE custody. "They are picking up law-abiding citizens. They're destroying families, jobs," he said."Go after the criminals. We're all for that. But leave the mom and pops and the kids alone. Man, he's destroying families," Gannon added.The Department of Homeland Security made an example out of Suarez and urged aliens not to make the mistake she did. "A pending immigration application does NOT confer legal status. ICE arrested Yasmin Suarez Reyes, an illegal alien from Venezuela, after she overstayed her lawful admission to the U.S. by OVER 2 YEARS. Don’t be like Yasmin — take advantage of our CBP Home offer and get $2,600 AND a FREE flight home," the DHS said.The arrest and the warning by the DHS mean you can enter the country legally and then apply for asylum when your visa period is over. But this pending application does not make you a legal resident -- you can be arrested.In an interview with CBS, Yasmin's fiancé Gannon said they were planning to travel from Houston to Las Vegas for a furniture industry convention.Gannon owns more than 1,000 billboards in the U.S. as well as several establishments in Mexico, including a hotel and a restaurant. After going through security at Houston's George Bush Intercontinental Airport, Gannon said his fiancée was arrested by agents in plainclothes.Yasmin entered the US legally in October 2023 under the Visa Waiver Program. Since she has citizenship of Spain, she was allowed to come to the US as a tourist without requiring a visa. Over 40 countries have this arrangement with the US and their nationals can enter the US for tourism without a visa and can stay up to 90 days. Yasmin applied for asylum in January 2024 before her stay validity lapsed. But that asylum case remained pending while she got a work permit and a driver's license in Texas.
Article Summary: 45-year-old Yasmin Suarez Reyes, a Venezuelan woman and a citizen of Spain, was arrested in July for overstaying her visa. Texas businessman John Gannon, 75, said he had been a lifelong Republican but now regreted voting for President Donald Trump as his fiancée is in ICE custody.

Article Title: California lost as many as 1.3 million Joshua trees in the 2020 Dome Fire; new software now helps park managers target recovery after wildfires
Article Text:
Digital tools deployed to rebuild desert ecosystems after destructive fires

Dystopian landscapes demand swift intervention

Adapting satellite technology for desert terrain

Scenario modeling directs limited conservation resources

California lost as many as 1.3 million Joshua trees when the 43,000-acre (17,400-hectare) Dome Fire burned through the Mojave National Preserve in 2020.According to the University of California, Berkeley, scientists at the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center for Data Science & Environment (DSE) have partnered with the US National Park Service to develop digital fire recovery tools. The new software helps park managers quickly map fire damage and focus restoration work on areas where fragile desert plants are most likely to survive.When UC Berkeley postdoctoral researchers Maya Zomer and Lucia Layritz travelled through burned parts of the Mojave National Preserve after the 2020 fire, they saw miles of charred vegetation that looked like a moonscape. Over time, the charcoal peeled away from burned Joshua trees, leaving behind white, skeleton-like trunks."It looks like a pretty dystopian landscape," Layritz said.Although researchers found green shoots and wildflowers growing through the sun-bleached soil, the plants face difficult chances of survival. Joshua trees (Yucca brevifolia and Yucca jaegeriana) can grow up to 40 feet (12 metres) tall and live for more than a century, but they can take up to 70 years to reach reproductive maturity.A 2019 study led by the University of California, Riverside, warned that rising temperatures and longer droughts caused by greenhouse gas emissions could wipe out Joshua trees across most of their historic range in Joshua Tree National Park by the end of the century.These climate pressures are made worse by invasive, non-native grasses. The weeds fill the gaps between desert shrubs, creating a continuous layer of dry fuel that allows large, intense fires to spread across landscapes that did not historically experience frequent fires."The frequency, magnitude and spatial area of the burns have definitely experienced a huge ramp-up in the last eight to 10 years within the greater Mojave Desert," said Maya Weltman-Fahs, a senior program manager at the Berkeley research center.Weltman-Fahs said most fires in the region are started by human activity, including recreational camping."People were very concerned," Layritz said. "It was like, OK, are we, I don't know, five big fires away from destroying the majority of the Joshua trees? And what do we do if that happens?"Unlike conifer forests, where standard satellite images can easily tell the difference between burned trees and healthy forest, desert ecosystems are much harder to study from space. Sparse vegetation and exposed rocky ground often reduce the accuracy of standard satellite burn measurements, making it difficult for park officials to quickly assess damage and apply for federal funding before restoration opportunities are lost."The desert ecosystems are very different from, say, a burned versus an unburned forest and what that would look like from satellite imagery," Weltman-Fahs said. "The desert had not been well-served by the existing comparative indices to examine the burn severity from satellite imagery. So that was the place that we started with our Joshua Tree partners—can we give you the information really quickly in the aftermath of a fire of what got burned, where, and how bad was it?"The team developed the DSE Disturbance Severity Tool, a mapping program designed specifically for dry desert environments. The Park Service used the software after two recent fires in Joshua Tree National Park: the 200-acre (81-hectare) Eureka Fire and the 2025 Black Rock Fire, which burned 72 acres (29 hectares) near a campsite."We used DSE's Disturbance Severity Tool twice last year to assess post-fire conditions following the Eureka and Black Rock fires," said Nick Graver, botany and vegetation monitoring program lead at Joshua Tree National Park and a graduate student in UC Riverside's Department of Evolution, Ecology and Organismal Biology. "Combined with field assessments conducted by park biologists, it provided the foundation for evaluating fire severity and developing recovery plans for both incidents. "In addition to mapping fire damage, the Berkeley team created a predictive platform called Josh. The interactive website allows park managers to test different long-term restoration strategies before planting nursery-grown seedlings or installing protective cages to keep herbivores away."Josh is a scenario planning tool where you can play out different restoration strategies, like outplanting or herbivory protection, and understand what their potential is, especially when you consider climate change," Layritz said.The software focuses on high-elevation areas known as "climate refugia." These cooler locations are expected to provide the best long-term habitat for Joshua trees as global temperatures rise, but they also collect thick grass cover, making them especially vulnerable to severe fires."The Mojave Desert may be at a critical shift from small, patchy fires to continuous large fires," Zomer said. "That's the motivation of a lot of work we are doing."By combining immediate burn maps with the Josh simulation platform, field teams can identify exactly where to send ground crews for the greatest ecological benefit."Resource limitation can also refer to how many boots they have on the ground to actually be going out and planting seedlings and watering them and helping support their establishment," Weltman-Fahs said. "If they're going to put forth that effort, they want to have a science-based, defensible reason to do that here rather than here."The research center plans to improve the software so local park officials can run recovery models on their own as soon as future wildfires occur.
Article Summary: California lost as many as 1.3 million Joshua trees when the 43,000-acre (17,400-hectare) Dome Fire burned through the Mojave National Preserve in 2020. The new software helps park managers quickly map fire damage and focus restoration work on areas where fragile desert plants are most likely to survive.

Article Title: A Cumberland mother's new farm stand was stolen before she could use it; strangers John and Casey Adams rebuilt it for free, even after their tools were stolen
Article Text:
Father-son build new farm stand for woman after stand stolen on her first day of business

Months of planning vanished overnight

Builders overcome tool theft to complete project

Security upgrades prepare business for launch

A mother of two who spent months preparing to open a home-based sourdough bakery had her brand-new farm stand stolen on its first night outside, but a father-and-son construction team of complete strangers rebuilt the entire stand for free, reports WJAR.Katrina Blancaflor, a former professional pastry chef, placed the wooden stand at the end of her driveway on the evening before 4 July to attract visitors from a local holiday road race. By the next morning, the stand had disappeared.When neighbours checked private security camera footage, the video showed an SUV arriving at 2:00 a.m., lifting the heavy wooden stand onto its roof, and driving away into the night.After Blancaflor shared the theft on social media, local builders John Adams and his son, Casey Adams, owners of Adams Construction in Cumberland, saw the post and offered to rebuild the stand without charging for labour or materials.Blancaflor trained at culinary school and worked at well-known restaurants, including Bobby Flay's restaurant in Las Vegas and David Burke's Primehouse in Chicago. After taking time away from her career to raise her two children, she began developing sourdough recipes at home and decided to start a small bakery called K's Bakestand.Her husband, Ian Swett, spent months designing and building a custom wooden roadside stand using detailed architectural drawings."It wasn't that easy. She's been on me since the winter to build this and life's busy, so, it was one of those projects that I kind of got procrastinating on until the Fourth of July," said Swett.The couple placed the stand outside on 3 July at 5:00 p.m. to promote upcoming pre-orders to workers driving home and runners taking part in the annual holiday race passing their property the next morning. Blancaflor’s daughter, Kalia, also planned to use part of the stand to sell squishies."I look up and it's not there and I have a little shock and then I'm like, well, there's no way somebody would've taken this," Swett recalled about the moment he stepped outside with his morning coffee on 4 July. "I figured, maybe she put it in the garage or something so I went and checked and it wasn't there."Blancaflor reported the theft to local police after neighbours shared street camera footage showing the 2:00 a.m. incident, but no arrests or recoveries were made immediately."At least three people on this road reached out with footage," said Blancaflor. "The fact it was at 2 a.m. was just really sketchy."After seeing the family's story online, John Adams offered to build a replacement stand using Swett's original design plans. Adams, who has run his residential construction company for 50 years with the slogan "Not A Problem," believed his team could rebuild it faster than the family could begin again."We thought, it's easier for us then for the husband to do it again," said Adams. "I wanted to duplicate it as best I could. The way he did it, he did a beautiful job and we did the best we could."The rebuild faced an unexpected problem when thieves broke into Adams Construction and stole the crew's tools during the project. Despite the delay, the builders replaced their equipment and completed the stand one week later than planned."Something like that, where it's not a big deal to us but a huge deal to them," said Casey Adams. "She came up and gave us a huge hug, and it was just like, you could tell it meant so much to her and really that's what it was all about."The Adams family delivered the finished stand directly to Blancaflor’s driveway, giving her an exact replacement of the original design."I was so shocked it literally brought tears to my eyes and when we saw it we were like wow, that looks just like our stand because I sent him the drawings that my husband did and it meant so much," Blancaflor said.K's Bakestand is now officially open and taking online pre-orders for local pickup. To prevent another theft, the family has installed a dedicated security camera system around the driveway, and Blancaflor has promised the Adams family free baked goods whenever they visit.
Article Summary: Katrina Blancaflor spent months preparing to open a home-based sourdough bakery. Her husband, Ian Swett, spent months designing and building a custom wooden roadside stand. The couple placed the stand outside on 3 July at 5:00 p.m. to promote upcoming pre-orders. The next morning, the stand had disappeared.

Article Text:
Billionaire Michael Moritz's newest bet to transform San Francisco is being driven by Crankstart – a private family foundation.

Structured evaluation process for global applicants

Initial registration and submission: Applicants must register through the competition portal by September 11, with full proposals due by October 9.
