It’s about putting Bangladesh back on right track,” she said, virtually addressing a press meet at Delhi’s Foreign Correspondents’ Club to mark the 2024 ‘July Uprising’ that led to her ouster from Bangladesh.Amid Dhaka’s outrage, Awami League said the house of cricketer Shakib Al Hasan, who attended the meet, was “attacked” back home.Fear cannot decide my duty to my people, and I will return to them in Dec. I am returning,” she said, combatively responding to statements of BNP functionaries that the Awami League chief would be arrested as soon as she lands in Dhaka.In a statement, the Bangladesh foreign ministry said it’s “outraged that absconding convicted genocider” Hasina was allowed to engage in a live interaction with media in New Delhi, where “she and her henchmen launched venomous vitriol against Bangladesh and her people”. “Dhaka deeply regrets that despite concerns conveyed a priori to the government of India about likely ramifications of this event on reset of our bilateral relations, this public event was permitted to be held,” it said.The exiled former PM struck a tough note in her first group interaction with media since she was forced to flee. She termed the “July Uprising” as a regime change operation and cited a statement of her sworn rival and former head of the stop-gap regime that took over from her. “(Muhammad) Yunus had himself said the protests were meticulously designed by a mastermind. His own words expose the truth. It wasn’t simply a spontaneous student protest. There was no visible or responsible leadership. Instructions were given invisibly,” she told the news conference.While other speakers, including her son Sajeeb Wazed Joy, were on video, she didn’t go into video mode at the presser, which was supposed to be her first public appearance after her ouster.Urging the international community to support “people’s struggle for democracy”, Hasina said Bangladesh’s future depends on restoration of democratic institutions, and outlined several demands, including “lifting ban on Awami League, releasing political prisoners, withdrawing false cases, restoring freedom of speech and media freedom, guaranteeing judicial independence, and ensuring law enforcement agencies serve people”.Bangladesh’s situation “is not only a domestic crisis; it affects regional peace, security, development and human dignity”, Hasina said. When asked about a specific time and date, Hasina said, “I just declared that I am coming. I’m going to Bangladesh. Now, date and everything, of course, when the time comes, I will tell everybody. I believe that the people of Bangladesh have suffered a lot and that’s why I decided to go back. The month of December is Bangladesh’s ‘Victory Month’. So, I want to go back in the month of December,” she said.
Article Summary: Bangladesh foreign ministry said it’s “outraged that absconding convicted genocider’ Hasina was allowed to engage in a live interaction with media in New Delhi. “I may be detained. I may be sent to prison. I am returning,” she said, combatively responding to statements of BNP functionaries that she would be arrested.

Article Title: 'Tried to set it on fire': Shakib Al Hasan’s house attacked after he attends Hasina's presser
Article Text:
Former Bangladesh captain Shakib Al Hasan's Magura residence came under attack, with police saying miscreants vandalised the house and attempted to set it ablaze.

Hours after former Bangladesh cricket captain and ex-lawmaker Shakib Al Hasan attended a media interaction addressed by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi, unidentified people allegedly attacked his house in Bangladesh's Magura district, police said.The incident took place around 9pm at Shakib's residence in the Keshab Mor area of Magura town, according to Md Abdullah Al Mamun, officer-in-charge of Magura Sadar Police Station.“Several miscreants threw brick chips at the house and vandalised windows. They also tried to set the house on fire,” the police officer told The Daily Star. No injuries were reported.Police said the identities of those involved were not immediately known. Security personnel have since been deployed around the property, and an investigation is underway.The attack came just hours after Shakib, who represented the Magura-1 constituency in Bangladesh's Parliament, participated in a media interaction hosted by the Foreign Correspondents' Club of South Asia in New Delhi. The event was addressed by Sheikh Hasina, who was ousted from power last year and has since been staying in India.Authorities have not officially linked the attack on Shakib's house to his appearance at the event, and no group has claimed responsibility for the incident.
Article Summary: Shakib Al Hasan's Magura residence attacked by miscreants, police say. Incident took place just hours after he attended media interaction in New Delhi. No injuries were reported, and no group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Security personnel have been deployed around the property.
